A Catalytic Highly Enantioselective Allene 
Approach to Oxazolines 
Hongwen Luo, b,† Zheng Yang, a† Weilong Lin, a,† Yangguangyan Zheng, c and Shengming 
Maa,c* 
Oxazolines are a very important class of heterocyclic compounds. However, catalytic 
enantioselective syntheses are very limited. Here, a highly enantioselective palladiumk
catalyzed couplingkcyclization of readily available 
Nk(butak2,3kdienyl) amides with aryl or 1k
alkenyl iodides has been developed for the asymmetric construction of oxazoline derivatives. 
Many synthetically useful functional groups are tolerated in this reaction. The absolute 
configuration of the chiral center in the products has been established by Xkray diffraction 
study. A model for prediction of the absolute configuration of the chiral center in the products 
from this cyclic enantioselective nucleophilic allylation has been proposed. The synthetic 
potentials based on the unique structure of the products formed have also been demonstrated. 
 
 
Introduction 
As a very important class of heterocyclic compounds, optically 
active oxazoline is not only present in many biologically active 
natural and unnatural compounds
1k7 (Scheme 1), but also a very 
versatile functional group in organic synthesis. 8k11 
 
Scheme 1. Oxazoline natural products and drug. Selected examples of natural 
products and drugs containing oxazoline with chiral centers at 4k or 5kposition. 
 They are usually synthesized from stoichiometric amounts 
of optically active amino alcohols, which instead are prepared 
from optically active amino acids. However, catalytic 
enantioselective approaches to optically active oxazolines are 
still very limited. Enantioselective alkylation of oxazolines 
under the catalysis of optically active phasektransfer catalyst
12k
14 and desymmetrization of Nk(1,3kdihydroxyk2kalkyl) amides15 
have been developed for the synthesis of optically active 
oxazolines with a chiral central at the 4kposition. 
Enantioselective reactions of oxazolines,
16k18 mesokaziridines,19 
and 2kisocyanocarbozylates20k27 have been realized by applying 
different chiral catalysts for the synthesis of optically active 
oxazolines with chiral centrals at both 4k and 5kpositions. On 
the other hand, the rutheniumkcatalyzed chemok and enantiok
selective hydrogenation of the C=C bond in prekformed 
oxazoles with 50 atm of H
2
28 and enantioselective 
halocyclization of stereodefined Nk(2kalkenyl) amides with an 
organocatalys29k33 have been reported for oxazoline derivatives 
with a chiral central at the 5kposition (Scheme 2A). These two 
pioneering contributions suffer from limitation of the starting 
materials and products. Thus, due to the importance of 
oxazolines, development of new catalytic enantioselective 
protocols for the efficient preparation of optically active 
oxazolines from readily available common chemicals is of 
current interest. On the other hand, we have been interested in 
developing enantioselective cyclization of allenes with a 
nucleophilic functionality for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis 
of hetereocyclic compounds.
34k39 Based on our recent 
development of straightforward method for the synthesis of 
allenes,
40 we envisioned a catalytic enantioselective allene 
approach to this class of compounds via the inksitu generation 
of 2ksubstituted 
πkallylic palladium intermediate and 
subsequent intramolecular allylic trapping by the oxygen atom 
in the amide functionality.
40k43 Such an enantioselective 
allylation is challenging due to the presence of the 2ksubstituent 
(R’), which has greatly complicated the relative energy of the 
synk and antikπkallylic palladium intermediates (Scheme 2B).

Results 
Optimization of the reaction. Nk(Butak2,3kdienyl)amide 1a 
and iodobenzene 2a were selected for our preliminary study on 
asymmetric cyclizative coupling reaction. However, with the 
biarylkbased phosphine ligand (S)kSEGPHOS ( L1), the desired 
oxazoline 3aa was afforded in only 2% ee albeit a high yield. 
The reaction with other ligands, such as P,Pkligands ( L2kL4), 
P,Nkligands (L5kL6), and P,Okligand ( L7), still yielded almost 
a racemic product. To our delight, Trost ligands ( L8kL10)44k45 
performed better in this reaction, and L10 was found to be the 
best (Figure 3, For the results with more ligands, see 
Supplementary Figure S1 in the Supplementary Information).  
 
Scheme 3. The effect of ligands. L10 was found to be the best. 
 
Further screening on the effect of bases led to the observation 
that Cs2CO3 is the best (Table 1, for the results with more bases, 
see Supplementary Table S1 in the Supplementary 
Information).

enantioselectivity, we investigated the solvent effect (Table 2). 
Other halogenkcontaining solvents such as 1,1kdichloroethane 
and 1,1,1ktrichloroethane failed to provide better results (Table 
2, entries 1 and 2). Etheric solvents such as DME, THF, MTBE, 
and dixoane also failed to improve the enantioselectivity (Table 
2, entries 3k6). Interestingly, when aromatic solvents were 
employed, higher enantioselectivity was constantly observed 
(Table 2, entries 7k11, 79%~88% 
ee) albeit with some recovery 
of 1a. It is surprising that the reaction with a slightly higher

Substrate Scope. With the optimized protocol in hand, we 
investigated the generality of this transformation. As shown in 
Table 3, a variety of optically active oxazoline derivatives 
could be prepared: 
Nk(butak2,3kdienyl)amides 1 with R 1 being 
electronkdonating substituents, such as 2k or 4kmethyl and 4k
methoxy groups, performed well with iodobenzene, affording 
the desired oxazoline products 
3bak3da with 64k82% yields and 
93k96% ees. Synthetically attractive halogen groups (F, Cl, Br) 
in substrates 1 were also tolerated in this reaction with high 
yields and ee values. The reaction of alkenyl or heteroaromatic 
substituted amides proceeded smoothly to afford the 
corresponding products 
3ha or 3ia in 71% and 88% yields, 
88% and 81% ees, respectively. For aryl iodides, different 
electronkdonating groups (Me, iPr, OMe) or Ph ( 2bk2g) were 
tolerated with very limited influence on the yields and 
enantioselectivity (73k84% yields, 93k96% 
ees). When 4k
acylphenyl iodide 2n was subjected to the reaction, the 
corresponding oxazoline 3an was obtained in 75% yield and 
88% ee. Halogen group (F, Cl, Br)ksubstituted aryl iodides 2 
are also suitable for this transformation, affording oxazoline 
derivatives 
3ahk3am in 77k86% yields and 91k94% ees. 
Sensitive functional groups such as primary amine ( 2o), ester 
(2p), and aldehyde group ( 2q) could be tolerated. It should be 
noted that the steric effect in those two starting materials does 
not affect the enantioselectivity. The absolute configuration of 
3ga with L10 was established as S by singlekcrystal Xkray 
diffraction study.46   
We also tried the reaction of  nonkterminal allenes1n and1o with 
phenyl iodide, however, neither of them afforded the corresponding 
oxazoline product (Scheme 4).

Discussion 
A model for the prediction of absolute configuration in the 
products with the Trost ligand L10 is shown below: oxidative 
addition of Pd(0) with iodobenzene 2a and subsequent 
carbopalladation with Nk(butak2,3kdienyl)amide 1a would form 
two πkallylic palladium intermediates A or B. The intermediates 
A is preferred over B due to the steric interaction of the amide 
group with the axial phenyl group, thus, subsequent 
nucleophilic Okattack in intermediate A (path a) leads to the 
product 3aa with the observed Skconfiguration (Scheme 7). In 
addition, the formation of the sevenkmembered product 7 is 
disfavored for the longer distance of nucleophilic Okcentered 
nucleophile as compared to that for the formation the 5k
membered 
3aa (path a vs. path b). 
 
Scheme 7. A proposed mechanism and prediction of the absolute 
configuration of the product. Due to the steric interaction of the amide group 
with the axial phenyl group, the product 3aa was observed with the absolute Sk
configuration. 
Stirring racemic 3al under the optimized reaction system for 
24 hours, no ee was detected with the recovered oxazoline, 
which means that the allylic cleavage in rack3al is not possible 
(Scheme 8). 
 
Scheme 8 Mechanistic study. No ee was detected with the recovered oxazoline, 
which means that the  nucleophilic Okattack in intermediate A of the mechanistic 
proposal is irreversible. 
Conclusion 
In conclusion, we have developed a completely different 
approach for the asymmetric construction of oxazoline 
derivatives with an excellent enantioselectivity via the 
palladiumkcatalyzed couplingkcyclization of 
Nk(butak2,3k
dienyl)amides with aryl iodides. The easily accessible and 
diversified nature of both starting materials,
40,50 the 
compatibility of useful functional groups, generality, and the 
synthetic potentials of the oxazoline and C=C bond make this 
method of high interest to both organic and medicinal chemists. 
Further studies in this area are being actively pursued in out 
laboratory.
